questions.q: Which branch should an Azure Pipelines release artifact point at?
options: The publish branch (adf_publish by default), not the collaboration branch
The collaboration branch (main) directly
Any feature branch currently open
It doesn't matter which branch is selected
questions.explain: The release artifact pulls from the publish branch, which holds the generated ARMTemplateForFactory.json and its parameters file — not the collaboration branch where development happens.

questions.q: What are the two key files generated in the publish branch that the deployment task uses?
options: ARMTemplateForFactory.json and ARMTemplateParametersForFactory.json
package.json and package-lock.json
pipeline.yaml and variables.yaml
A single combined factory.json file
questions.explain: The ARM Template Deployment task points at ARMTemplateForFactory.json for the template itself and ARMTemplateParametersForFactory.json for the environment-specific parameter values.

questions.q: What's the real danger of using Complete deployment mode instead of Incremental?
options: Complete mode deletes any resource in the resource group that isn't present in the new template
Complete mode is simply slower, with no functional difference
Complete mode can't deploy triggers at all
There's no real difference between the two modes
questions.explain: In Complete deployment mode, resources that exist in the target resource group but aren't specified in the new ARM template get deleted — a genuinely dangerous setting to get wrong in production.

questions.q: Why can a deployment fail when a trigger is currently active?
options: Data Factory can't update a trigger definition while it's actively running/enabled
Active triggers are automatically excluded from every deployment with no issue
Triggers can never be deployed via ARM templates at all
This only affects tumbling window triggers, not schedule triggers
questions.explain: Deployment can fail outright when trying to update an active trigger, which is why a pre-deployment script stops triggers and a post-deployment script restarts them afterward.

questions.q: What does Microsoft's PrePostDeploymentScript.Ver2.ps1 do differently from a basic stop-all/start-all script?
options: It only stops and restarts triggers that actually changed, not every trigger in the factory
It deletes all triggers permanently before every deployment
It has nothing to do with triggers at all
It only works with tumbling window triggers
questions.explain: The Ver2 script is smart enough to target only the triggers that actually changed in that deployment, rather than stopping and restarting every trigger in the factory unnecessarily.
